title: Made an epic dark-fantasy redesign of Minecraft’s main menu - Skyborn
author: 1MB_Memory
selftext:
Here’s the first mod from **Skyborn**, a series of mods I’m making to gradually redesign Minecraft and add new features across different parts of the game.

So far I’ve only finished the main menu, which already establishes a lot of the visual language I’m aiming for, while the in-game features and 3D assets are still being shaped behind it.

The goal isn’t to turn Minecraft into something that’s constantly dark, hostile, and exhausting. **Skyborn is still meant to preserve and expand on the cozy, wholesome side of Minecraft too.** The darker and more epic parts are there to give the world more weight, flavor, and character without dismantling what already makes Minecraft feel like Minecraft. There should still be that sense of having a home to come back to.

For the visuals, I usually start by roughly shaping the composition myself, blocking out where I want the mountains, ruins, character, sky, clouds, and everything else to sit, color coding them and then use generative AI to help turn those rough shapes into the actual assets. After that I separate everything back into layers and rebuild the scene inside the mod, allowing the different depths to move independently and create the parallax effect you see in the video. So it ends up being a back and forth between rough composition, generation, cutting things into usable assets, layering, and then making everything move together.

The menu also starts establishing the lore of this version of Minecraft. Its original song is **written in Ancient Greek and sung using reconstructed Ancient Greek pronunciation**, telling the basic backstory of the world.

The lore itself is pretty simple: the world went to sh\*t because of the Dragon, and many years later the **Skyborn came down from the sky**. A little cheesy, but that’s half the fun of fantasy.

Mostly posting it here because people here might actually be interested in the workflow too, and I’d like to get some opinions on both the direction and how it all comes together in motion.
